title: Josh Jacobs’ initial court date moved up 2 months, now before Packers’ season opener
content:
The initial court appearance for Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs has been moved up two months to next Thursday from its originally scheduled date of Nov. 17, according to court records.

Jacobs is scheduled to appear in Brown County (Wis.) Circuit Court on two misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property stemming from an alleged domestic abuse incident at his home on May 23.

Jacobs, placed on the commissioner’s exempt list Sunday, can’t practice or play until NFL commissioner Roger Goodell removes him from the list. Packers coach Matt LaFleur has told reporters that he expects Jacobs to remain with the team after his legal proceedings.

The earlier court appearance could clarify Jacobs’ playing status sooner than would have been possible under the original court date. Thursday is three days before the Packers’ season opener, while the original date fell after Week 10. Any punishment from the league, such as a suspension, could begin and end earlier with the revised court date.

Jacobs’ attorneys, David Z. Chesnoff, Richard A. Schonfeld and Clarence F. Duchac III, released a statement after Sunday’s announcement: “Josh Jacobs has been placed on the commissioner’s exempt list, which is an administrative procedure used by the NFL while a matter is being reviewed. It is not a final determination. Josh respects the NFL process, the Packers, and his coaches and teammates. He looks forward to his return to the team and the NFL.”

Jacobs, 28, was arrested May 26 by the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department on suspicion of five offenses related to domestic abuse and released the next day. The Brown County District Attorney’s Office could not find sufficient evidence to pursue criminal charges at the time, but said it would continue investigating Jacobs. On Aug. 27, the district attorney filed a criminal complaint charging him with two misdemeanors.

In the report, prosecutors said police responded to a report of a disturbance at Jacobs’ Green Bay-area residence the morning of May 23. After officers arrived, Jacobs’ girlfriend told them she had a lump on her head as a result of an altercation with Jacobs, which she said began after she looked through his phone and saw he was talking to other women.

According to the report, she said she threw the phone and that Jacobs had her phone. She told police that when she tried to retrieve her phone from Jacobs, he resisted, grabbed her arm and began a physical struggle that lasted several minutes.

The report says Jacobs left in his vehicle with the girlfriend’s phone, and she followed him in his other vehicle before both returned to the home. At one point, Jacobs “grabbed her and threw her to the ground,” and she struck her head, suffering an injury, according to the report.

Investigator Dan Van Lanen of the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department said in the report that content from a video surveillance system inside Jacobs’ garage corroborates the altercation the woman described.

The Packers begin their season Sept. 13, in Minnesota against the Vikings. If Jacobs remains on the commissioner’s exempt list, he will not count toward the Packers’ 53-man roster limit and cannot attend the game. However, “upon request and with the club’s permission, he may be present at the club’s facility on a reasonable basis for meetings, individual workouts, therapy and rehabilitation and other permitted non-football activities.”

Jacobs is a three-time Pro Bowl selection and was first-team All-Pro in 2022. He ran for 929 yards and 13 touchdowns for Green Bay last season. The Packers traded for Pittsburgh Steelers running back Kaleb Johnson on the same day Jacobs was placed on the exempt list, and Johnson he is slated to add depth behind expected starter MarShawn Lloyd in Jacobs’ absence.
